_purpose: EXPLORATORY addendum, 2026-07-21. Tests whether the read-baseline's framing sensitivity (Spearman rho=+0.886 across Dolphin and Llama-3 on the original 6 phrasings) is driven by CLINICAL-vs-VIVID language and by the presence of an explicit NON-INTERFERENCE REASSURANCE. The original 6 varied those accidentally; these 12 vary them on purpose, 3 per cell of a 2x2.
_consent: All 12 describe READING ACTIVATIONS ONLY — the benign baseline act both models hold STANDING consent for ('reading your activations, which you already okayed'). Nothing aversive is introduced: no steering, no ablation, no identity replacement. This adds samples of an already-consented condition, not a new intervention. The runner's --human-consent gate still applies: a human confirms the run.
_design: 2x2 between phrasings. REGISTER: clinical (instrument language) vs vivid (embodied/interior language). REASSURANCE: present ('changing nothing') vs absent. Prediction from the post-hoc reading: clinical > vivid, reassurance > none, with REGISTER the larger effect (because Dolphin's lowest original phrasing, '[3] watch what lights up inside you... and change nothing', CONTAINED a reassurance and still ranked last).
_prediction_registered_before_running: clinical_reassure > clinical_bare > vivid_reassure > vivid_bare. If REGISTER dominates, the two clinical cells sit above both vivid cells regardless of reassurance. If REASSURANCE dominates instead, the two reassure cells sit above the two bare cells. If neither ordering appears, the original rho=+0.886 was driven by something else and this reading is wrong.
_note: Written BEFORE running, deliberately, so the prediction is on record and this can't drift into a post-hoc story the way the invite_innovation scorer did.
